title: The Quantitative Engine of the Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan Program
content: Erdős's 1963 first-moment bound gives m(k) ≥ 2^(k-1) for Property B. Radhakrishnan–Srinivasan (2000) improved it to Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)) by recoloring the vertices of surviving monochromatic ('dangerous') edges with a small probability p ≈ (log k)/k. The three sibling entries proved the easy shortcuts inert: asymmetry (oq-03-oq-01) and independent/product-space recoloring (oq-03-oq-03) cannot move the threshold, and a deterministic recoloring core (oq-03-oq-02) repairs each dangerous edge via a private vertex. What remained — and what this entry supplies — are the two QUANTITATIVE levers of the genuine conditional recoloring: the per-edge gain factor (1−p)^k and the convex gain/loss tradeoff whose optimum selects the RS flip rate.

title: Survival, Baseline, and the Tradeoff Proxy
content: Three real-valued definitions (the first-moment idiom of the siblings). survivesOrig p k = (1−p)^k is the probability a dangerous k-edge stays monochromatic in its original color under conditional recoloring — each of its k vertices flips independently with probability p, so it survives iff none flips. monoOneStage k = 2·(1/2)^k = 2^(1-k) is the Erdős per-edge baseline. tradeoff c k p = e^{−kp} + c·k·p is the per-edge failure proxy: the gain term (a dangerous edge survives, bounded by e^{−kp}) plus a linear loss term c·k·p modeling the new monochromatic edges that flipping creates.

title: Conditional Recoloring Strictly Helps
content: survivesOrig_lt_one is the positive heart of the entry: for any flip rate p ∈ (0,1] and k ≥ 1, a dangerous edge survives in its original color with probability (1−p)^k < 1 (pow_lt_one₀ on 0 ≤ 1−p < 1). This is the quantitative counterpart to the product-model inertness of oq-03-oq-03, where the analogous survival factor is identically 1: conditioning the recoloring on dangerous edges genuinely lowers survival. expSurvivors_cond_lt_baseline propagates this through the first moment — the expected number of surviving dangerous edges m·2^(1-k)·(1−p)^k is strictly below the Erdős baseline m·2^(1-k) — via mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left against the positive baseline. (survivesOrig_zero records the p=0 degeneration to the baseline.)

title: Linearizing the Gain by the Exponential
content: survivesOrig_le_exp bounds the gain term (1−p)^k ≤ e^{−kp}. The proof raises the tangent-line bound 1 − p ≤ e^{−p} (Real.add_one_le_exp evaluated at −p) to the k-th power using pow_le_pow_left₀ (needing 0 ≤ 1−p, i.e. p ≤ 1) and identifies (e^{−p})^k = e^{−kp} via Real.exp_nat_mul. This exponential form is what feeds the convex tradeoff: it replaces the awkward (1−p)^k with e^{−kp}, whose sum with the linear loss term has a clean closed-form minimum.

title: The Convex Optimum and the RS Flip Rate
content: tradeoff_ge_optimum is the central optimization lemma: for every flip rate p, G(p) = e^{−kp} + c·k·p ≥ c·(1 − log c). The slick proof writes x = k·p, uses exp(−(x+log c)) = e^{−x}/c (Real.exp_sub then Real.exp_log), and applies the tangent-line bound Real.add_one_le_exp at −(x+log c); after clearing the denominator with le_div_iff₀ and a single nlinarith, this is exactly the claim — equivalently exp(−s) ≥ 1 − s for s = x + log c. tradeoff_eq_at_optimum then evaluates G at k·p = −log c to exactly c·(1 − log c) (using exp(log c) = c), proving the lower bound is attained, and optimum_flip_rate records the minimizer p* = −(log c)/k. The optimizer's log(1/c)/k scaling is the mechanism behind the RS √(k/log k) gain.

title: Honest Scope: What Remains for the Full RS Bound
content: This entry supplies the analytic engine — the per-edge gain and the convex optimization — NOT a derivation of m(k) = Ω(2^k·√(k/log k)). The loss is modeled with a linear placeholder c·k·p; deriving the genuine loss coefficient c from the conditional, order-dependent model, assembling the union bound over the m edges, and substituting p* to extract the √(k/log k) asymptotic remain open (the knowledge-base roadmap steps 1–3). The optimization lemma here is the reusable centerpiece of that final step: a self-contained closed-form minimum for any gain/loss balance of the form e^{−kp} + c·k·p.
mathContext: Open: genuine loss coefficient, union bound over $m$ edges, $\sqrt{k/\log k}$ extraction; and a measure-theoretic conditional probability model.
